bug_semantics: keras.models.load_model() on a malicious .keras archive: the H5 path resolves weights through H5IOStore/ShardedH5IOStore.__getitem__ (keras/src/saving/saving_lib.py), which after link/dtype validation calls np.array(value) on the h5py Dataset — materializing the FULL declared shape in memory with no bound on the allocation. A crafted .keras (or its inner model.weights.h5) with a chunked/compressed/fill-value-only dataset (or any dataset whose declared size the pre-existing guards do not reach: below the 4 GiB floor, within the 1000x expansion ratio, or shaped to exhaust memory through the 8-byte-per-element bfloat16/other-dtype path) forces an unbounded allocation and OOM-kills the loader (exit code 137) — denial of service, CWE-770. The advisory states this bypasses the CVE-2026-0897 fix, which had only covered the same allocation pattern inside KerasFileEditor (PR #21880, f704c887), not the main load_model path.
flaw_origin: Commit a762b418bfc162d16b92670d938d53c28ad2766c ("Refactor handling of bfloat16 dtype in h5 files.", 2024-01-24, author/committer Francois Chollet <francois.chollet@gmail.com>) first wrote the unvalidated dataset-materialization sink: it introduced the H5Entry.__getitem__ that does `value = self.group[name]` (raw h5py subscript returning a lazy Dataset) followed by `np.array(value, dtype=ml_dtypes.bfloat16)` — the first unbounded np.array() materialization of an attacker-shaped h5 dataset on the model-load path; before this commit the h5 read path converted via backend.convert_to_tensor without materializing datasets here. The consuming H5IOStore.__getitem__ the advisory names descends from this sink through the weights-sharding rewrite d865f5f0f2b7 (2025-03-19, same np.array materialization) and the dict-methods commit 9286df3460cb (2025-06-11, added the `elif not isinstance(value, np.ndarray): value = np.array(value)` branch); both are recorded in decomposed_shas as the wave that carried the sink into H5IOStore/ShardedH5IOStore.__getitem__ verbatim.
